seeds.title: STILL SECTION

sections.s01_concept: Create a 2:3 vertical ultra-premium editorial design plate titled “STILL SECTION”, built as a flat graphic system with exactly one dimensionally rendered rectangular frame zone, featuring Hatsune Miku as the only character inside a flooded glass cistern shown as a clean architectural cross-section. Preserve her unmistakable canonical identity: luminous aqua eyes, straight aqua bangs, extremely long aqua twin tails, black-and-magenta square hair ornaments, youthful anime facial structure, slim proportions, and a clearly recognizable Hatsune Miku silhouette. Her face, eyes and hands must stay fully rendered and readable. This image is not a photograph of a printed sheet and not a mockup: it is the design itself on an abstract infinite plane.
sections.s14_graphics: Place Miku inside the frame at approximately thirty-three percent of the canvas, seen from a slightly low three-quarter angle, standing on a narrow ceramic ledge at the frame’s lower third. Her head, shoulders and hands remain above the water line. Her body continues past the frame’s bottom rule, and everything below that rule converts instantly into flat graphic language: a coarse halftone taper, a single-weight aqua contour and a blank pale field. The conversion happens exactly at the frame line, never fades, and never rises above her hips.
sections.s03_action: Give Miku exactly one core action built from two contacts. Her right hand is pushed into the water cut plane at chest height, so the palm and fingers are seen through water: magnified by about eight percent, offset sideways, softly doubled at the edges, and crossed by thin aqua caustic lines. Her left hand presses flat against the frame’s inner vertical edge from inside, fingertips just crossing the line; beyond that line the fingertips become three single-weight vector lines and stop. Add no second prop and no second action.
sections.s04_motif: Construct the dominant visual object as the cross-section of the colossal cistern itself: a flooded glass column cut cleanly open so the viewer looks straight through the cut face. Build the visible section from thick glass walls with rounded edges and bright rim highlights, a pale ceramic floor slab, cobalt weir plates at two heights, silver intake pipes, a pearl-white overflow lip and a single gold filament valve at the deepest point. The cut face must read as a flat aqua plane with refraction, while the volumes behind it carry suspended sediment, drifting particles and caustics.
sections.s11_costume: Dress Miku in a graphite and pearl immersion suit derived from her recognizable virtual-singer design language: a fitted bodice with aqua luminous seams, a short asymmetric skirt of ceramic plates, detached sleeves with fine black calibration lines, dark thigh-high elements, a narrow silver shoulder yoke, a transparent membrane forearm guard on her submerged arm, and exactly three tiny coral fasteners. The suit reads as laboratory formalwear, not a concert outfit.
sections.s05_material: Translate every material into one of two languages. Inside the frame, glass shows thick rims, double contours, internal bubbles and magnifying caustics; water shows surface tension, a visible cut edge, suspended particles and refracted displacement; ceramic shows a hard pale silhouette with a pearl glaze; cobalt enamel shows one opaque saturated plane with a narrow polished highlight; silver shows compressed reflection; gold filament appears only at the valve. Outside the frame, the same materials become flat spot-colour bands, single-weight contours, halftone and blank knockouts. Never let rendered optics leak outside the frame.
sections.s20_type: Integrate a strict typography system. Set the exact readable title “STILL SECTION” in a wide-letter-spaced condensed serif across the upper band, letting one letter cross the frame rule and invert to pale inside the rendered zone. Add “PLATE 04 / DEPTH 39” in small condensed sans beneath the title. Place “VOICE INDEX” vertically along the outer right edge, reading bottom to top. Every other string on the plate must be a short hexadecimal run, a numeric ladder or a corrupted glyph sequence that never resolves into readable words.
sections.s21_light: Light the plate in three tiers. Inside the frame use a cool white key from above the water, a bright caustic mesh projected onto her arms, throat and skirt, a narrow cobalt rim on her cheek and shoulder, and sharp white specular highlights on the glass rims and the water cut edge. On the flat field use no lighting at all: flat spot colours, flat halftone, flat linework. Add one thin luminous aqua seam along the frame rules so the transition reads as a designed cut.
sections.s22_layers: Maintain five readable layers. Layer one: the cropped foreground glass wall and one steel pipe entering from the lower left. Layer two: Miku’s face, submerged hand, pressed hand and the water cut plane. Layer three: the cistern interior, its nine strata and its caustics. Layer four: the flat field with halftone dissolution, construction grid, the nine aligned data bands and caption slots. Layer five: the outer margins with crop marks, registration targets and empty pale field.
sections.s23_medium: Render the result as a high-end editorial design plate rather than an illustration or a photographed object: flat spot-colour graphic system, vector-sharp linework, controlled halftone bands and one dimensionally rendered window of glass, water, ceramic, enamel and silver. Give the finest linework to Miku’s face and hands, the richest optical detail to the water cut plane and the submerged hand, the strictest geometry to the frame, the strata alignment and the data column, and the most restrained treatment to the outer margins.
sections.s24_constraint: No additional characters, no duplicate Miku, no second face, no physical paper, no cardboard, no torn edge, no bevel, no drop shadow, no table, no mockup photograph, no pushpins, no paper clips, no staples, no tape, no stickers, no glass vials, no test tubes, no sample capsules, no glossy 3D scene across the whole plate, no cinematic depth of field, no bloom, no lens flare, no warm light, no rainbow palette, no random English words, no watermark, no signature, no text over her face, no halftone over her eyes or hands. Preserve a strict hierarchy: her face and the submerged palm first, the frame rule and pressed hand second, the nine strata and cistern section third, the aligned data bands and typography fourth, then the flat field and empty margins.
sections.s25_closing: The final image should feel like an engineering plate that has been submerged: one drawn frame opens onto a cut cistern, a girl stands half in water and half in graphic space, one palm is seen refracted through the cut face while the other pushes against the design boundary itself, nine sediment layers descend into pure blankness, and the nine data bands outside the frame measure exactly the water they came from. Flat spot-colour editorial system, one dimensional section, layered luxury materials, aggressive interlocking occlusion, dense but governed ornament, no physical props, premium Krea 2 key visual, and a composition that reads as designed rather than photographed.

extra: Keep the whole field outside the frame as pure graphic space: a clean pale cool-white surface with no paper fibre, no grain, no folds, no torn edges, no bevel, no drop shadow, no table, no studio light. Every graphic edge is vector-sharp. The only permitted texture is an intentional halftone field used as a graphic element.

Draw the frame as pure linework at roughly sixty-two percent of the canvas, offset slightly right of centre: one six-pixel cobalt rule, one one-pixel graphite rule inside it, and four sharp corner brackets. No thickness, no rounded corners, no inner bevel, no shadow, no paper lip. Inside the frame the interior field is a pale aqua plane and the image becomes optically three-dimensional; outside the frame everything stays flat graphic. The frame must look placed by a designer, not cut from cardboard.

Divide the interior into nine horizontal sediment strata that run the full width of the frame, each with a different thickness and edge behaviour. From the surface downward: clear aqua water with a bright caustic mesh; a fine silt band with soft diffused edges; a cobalt-dyed layer with one sharp boundary; a ceramic shard bed with hard chipped silhouettes; a frosted salt crust with crystalline edges; a wireframe pipe section rendered only as geometry; a halftone band with a visible dot gradient; a white knockout band where the water simply stops being drawn; and an empty pale field at the bottom that matches the surrounding graphic space exactly.

Make those nine strata and the data column one single system: every stratum continues outside the frame as a flat horizontal band of exactly the same height, so the right side of the plate reads as the measured index of the water it just left. The alignment must be exact and visible; this rhyme is the core design idea of the image.

Establish complex interlocking occlusion. One thick foreground glass wall edge, cropped by the left frame rule, passes in front of her right shoulder. A silver intake pipe passes in front of her left hip and behind the cobalt weir. The water cut plane sits in front of her torso from the waist down, so her lower body is visibly read through liquid. Her face, eyes and both hands remain completely unobstructed by glass, pipe or water.

Build the right-hand data column from nine flat bands of equal height, aligned to the strata: the first holds a short hexadecimal string, the second a numeric ladder of ticks, the third a flat raster chip of aqua pixels, the fourth a corrupted run of unreadable glyphs, the fifth a bracket-enclosed code pair, the sixth a regular dot matrix, the seventh a small error flag, the eighth an intentionally empty band, and the ninth a single acid-yellow tick. No capsules, no vials, no glass discs, no pins, no clips, no staples, no tape and no stickers anywhere.

Let her hair behave like another fluid layer. The upper twin tail rises out of the water, passes behind a glass rim, and where it leaves the frame it becomes a clean aqua contour following one construction column. The lower twin tail sinks below the water line, refracts into a doubled offset shape, thins into suspended strands and terminates as three short dashes. Keep the hair fully rendered and saturated around her head.

Use a cool palette with no warm paper tone. Approximately thirty-eight percent pale cool white and pearl white, twenty percent prussian blue, sixteen percent aqua and icy cyan, eight percent cobalt, eight percent graphite, five percent silver and mirror highlight, three percent acid yellow, one percent coral, one percent pale grey. Acid yellow appears only as one error flag, one scale pointer and one deep valve highlight. No cream, no beige, no orange, no magenta field.

Apply graphic-system devices instead of print-physical effects: sharp corner crop marks, two registration targets, one deliberate one-and-a-half-millimetre plate offset appearing only in flat zones, a knocked-out white text area in the header, and thin leader lines running from three stratum boundaries to small caption slots. No squeegee streaks, no ink absorption, no finger smudges, no fold memory, no paper texture.

seeds.title: VEIL FALL

sections.s01_concept: Create a wide 16:9 ultra-premium futuristic anime game key visual titled “VEIL FALL”, featuring Hatsune Miku as the only physical character walking through a colossal curtain of hanging glass filaments inside a white chamber. Preserve her unmistakable canonical identity: luminous aqua eyes, straight aqua bangs, extremely long aqua twin tails, black-and-magenta square hair ornaments, youthful anime facial structure, slim proportions, and a clearly recognizable Hatsune Miku silhouette. She must remain unmistakably Miku even while the veil surrounds her, and her face, eyes, hands and hair ornaments must stay readable through the filament density.
sections.s03_action: Give Miku exactly one core action built from two contacts. Her raised right forearm pushes a bundle of glass filaments aside so they part into a narrow vertical slit around her face and chest. Her left hand, at hip height, holds a single filament that runs taut back up to the rail, and one thickened glass bead is sliding down that filament, caught a few centimeters from her fingers. The sliding bead beside her hand is the tension point. Add no second prop and no second action.
sections.s04_motif: Construct the dominant visual object as a colossal curtain of hanging glass filaments that falls from a curved rail across the top of the frame, drops the entire height of the image at the tilted angle, and pools on a matte-black floor as a frosted drift. The curtain occupies approximately seventy-six percent of the canvas. Use roughly eight thousand filaments of sharply different thickness: the thickest read as clear glass rods, the middle ones as fine threads with beads, and the finest as pale hair lines. Crop the rail and the pooled hem at the frame edges so the curtain clearly exceeds the image.
sections.s05_material: Organize the curtain into eight horizontal bands of material progression from the rail down to the floor. The top band is taut clear glass with no beads. The second thickens slightly. The third grows isolated beads on the filaments at a consistent height. The fourth merges beads into long vertical capsules. The fifth fuses neighbouring capsules into a continuous clear sheet. The sixth frosts that sheet. The seventh thins it into a silver wireframe grid. The eighth dissolves the hem into clean cyan contours, cobalt pixel clusters and a few white gaps. Make every band horizontally readable so the veil reads as a single process from tension to absence.
sections.s06_sequence: Suspend nine glass tension weights from selected filaments just below the rail as the secondary repeated sequence. Each weight is a small tapered glass form on its own thread: a plain clear drop, a drop with one cobalt core line, a drop with trapped bubbles, a frosted drop, a drop with a hairline crack, a drop reduced to a silver shell, a drop reduced to a wireframe, an empty silver ring, and finally an empty ring holding only a shadow. Arrange them at intervals so they repeat without becoming a row.
sections.s10_hair: Let Miku’s hair behave like part of the veil. The upper twin tail rises behind her head, threads between two capsules, and reappears magnified inside the continuous clear sheet before ending as a clean aqua curve in the narrow white strip above the rail. The lower twin tail falls across the black floor, passes beneath the pooled hem, and separates into three fine cyan contours near the bottom edge. Keep the hair dense, solid and recognizable around her head with no filaments crossing her face.
sections.s11_costume: Dress Miku in a white, cobalt and graphite veil-walking suit derived from her recognizable virtual-singer design language. Use a fitted graphite bodice with aqua luminous seams, a narrow asymmetric skirt of layered ceramic plates over a transparent cyan underlayer, one detached sleeve with fine black calibration lines on the pushing arm and a bare microfiber-wrapped forearm on the other side, dark thigh-high elements with thin cobalt seams, a pearl-white collar piece, and exactly three tiny coral fasteners. Add one narrow glass-bead cuff at the wrist that holds the taut filament, and keep the whole costume light enough to pass between threads.
sections.s12_env: Build the environment as a compressed white chamber rather than an open void. Use one large matte-black floor plane occupying the bottom sixth of the frame, a broad cobalt wedge entering from the lower left, a tall translucent panel standing behind the veil, and two floating white slabs near the upper right. Preserve only about twenty-two percent clean white negative space, placed as a narrow strip above the rail, a thin triangle at the lower right, and the bright slit around her body. The tight negative space must feel like compressed air, not emptiness.
sections.s13_palette: Use a bolder color system than a calm white room. Approximately sixty percent of the image is pure white, pearl white and pale silver; fifteen percent is cobalt blue and deep ultramarine; twelve percent is aqua and icy cyan; six percent is true black and matte carbon, concentrated in the floor plane and the heaviest capsules; four percent is vivid acid yellow used only as the encoder tick line and one rail index; one percent is coral on the suit fasteners and one bead; half a percent is a single magenta registration sliver inside the wireframe band. Do not introduce any other warm hue.
sections.s16_mask: Apply aggressive but protected masks. Place one tall translucent cyan inverse mask over the lower half of the veil, one cobalt inverse plane behind the upper right drifting strand, a white knockout bar cutting horizontally through the sixth band, and one narrow mirror mask along the taut filament she holds. Where the lower twin tail crosses a cobalt mask, convert it into a white silhouette with a thin aqua outline. Where capsules overlap the encoder strip, magnify and bend the ticks beneath them. Masks may cover outer hair, skirt plates, legs, filaments, capsules, the hem and the rail bracket, but never her face, both eyes, hands, finger separations or the sliding bead.
sections.s20_type: Add a bold typography system rotated with the composition. Set the exact readable title “VEIL FALL” vertically, rotated to run down the bright slit beside her body, in an ultra-thin extended sans serif, with two filaments crossing in front of the letter F without making the word unreadable. Add “TENSION LOG / 08” in small condensed cobalt type along the rail. Place one outlined “39” emblem inside a white square beside the acid-yellow rail index. Include no other readable words; all remaining texture stays as abstract marks and ticks.
sections.s21_light: Illuminate the scene from behind the veil. Use a broad cold white backlight passing through the filaments so every thread glows at its edge, a concentrated aqua glow inside the continuous clear sheet, thin acid-yellow edge light along the encoder band, a narrow cobalt rim on Miku’s turned cheek and shoulder, and pale cyan caustics crawling across her pushing forearm and skirt. Let the matte floor absorb most of the light so the barcode shadow stays deep and clean. Avoid warm light, fog, haze, muddy grey shadows and uncontrolled bloom.
sections.s24_constraint: No additional physical characters, no duplicate Miku, no second face, no portrait panels, no natural landscape, no generic cyberpunk city, no fabric curtain, no silk or velvet, no water, no rain, no symmetrical angel pose, no ordinary feathered wings, no filament covering her face, no filament covering her eyes, no filament covering her hands, no melted glass, no rubbery strands, no spider web, no uncontrolled full-canvas glitch, no muddy grey background, no warm orange lighting, no rainbow palette, no random letters, no text over her face, no watermark. Preserve a strict hierarchy: Miku’s face and the sliding bead first, her pushing forearm and the parted slit second, the veil bands and encoder strip third, the tension weights and micro-ornament fourth, then typography, barcode shadow and the narrow white strips.
sections.s25_closing: The final image should feel like walking through a hanging instrument that measures tension while it is being pulled apart: eight thousand glass threads fall on a tilted rail, thicken into beads and capsules, fuse into a sheet, frost, thin into wireframe and let their hem dissolve, one encoder band turns the whole veil into a ruler, nine weights record the load, and a single girl pushes the filaments aside while one bead slides toward her fingers. extra: Tilt the entire composition: make the hanging rail run from the upper left down toward the right at roughly twenty-five degrees, so the whole room sits on a deliberate Dutch angle while Miku herself remains vertically upright inside it. Use a medium-wide lens from a slightly low position. Place her just right of center, full body from boots to hair ornaments, occupying approximately thirty percent of the frame. She steps forward out of the veil with her weight on the leading leg and her back shoulder turned, her head level, both aqua eyes clearly visible.

Build the rail as architecture, not a rod. Use a curved pearl-white ceramic beam, cobalt enamel brackets, black hinge plates, silver tension rings, and thin gold filigree seams, then let every filament hang from an individual silver ring so the top edge becomes a dense metallic fringe. The rail should read as a machined instrument that holds the veil under measurable tension.

Turn the curtain into a measuring instrument. Along one mid-height band, embed a fine horizontal encoder: a continuous row of tiny dark ticks of varying length across the filaments, interrupted every twelfth thread by a slightly thicker silver ring and a small cobalt index block. This barcode-like strip must run along the veil with the same twenty-five-degree tilt, and it must be physically tied to the filaments rather than pasted on top. It is the only place where the interface becomes the material itself.

Establish aggressive occlusion with at least three interlockings. A thick bundle of filaments passes in front of her skirt and left thigh, then behind her shoulder, then in front again at the far side. Two long capsules hang directly in front of one tension weight. The single taut filament she holds crosses in front of her forearm but never in front of her face. The slit that her forearm opens must expose her face and both eyes completely, as though her body has physically pushed the glass aside.

Give the veil two secondary gestures so it is not a flat wall. Let the pooled hem billow slightly to the left along the floor, pushed by her forward motion, and let a slower strand drift away from the curtain near the upper right, curving out of the main fall. Make that drifting strand carry the thinnest beads and the lightest cyan tint, so it reads as a stray note rather than a second curtain.

Use glitch collage as controlled material failure at the hem only. Concentrate horizontal displacement slices, cobalt rectangular masks, white erased blocks, cyan and acid-yellow channel offsets, pixel clusters, halftone fragments, duplicated contour echoes, photocopy grain and narrow black scan bars around the eighth band, the far-left end of the rail, the stray drifting strand and the outer twin-tail ends. Keep the rail, the first six bands, her body, her face and her hands physically coherent.

Add a heavy but precise layer of luxury micro-ornament at the rail and the bead line. Run silver rings at every twelfth filament, a string of tiny ceramic beads along one cobalt bracket, engraved gold filigree on exactly three rail seams, four clear droplets suspended under the lowest intact capsules, and two narrow vellum tags printed with abstract tension diagrams hanging from the rail. Add fine brass hinge pins and a few razor-thin glass slivers that catch the light like needles. Keep ornament off her face and hands.

Create a second composition through shadow and slit light, and make it louder than the first. Let the veil throw an enormous barcode shadow across the black floor, its stripes tilting with the Dutch angle and breaking where the eighth band has dissolved. Let the parted slit around her body cut one hard vertical beam of white light down the floor and up the far wall, crossing the shadow stripes at a clean angle. Let the encoder strip cast a thin ladder of tick shadows onto her forearm and collar.

Maintain five readable depth layers. Foreground: one thick bundle of filaments, two large capsules and the taut filament she holds, all crossing the frame at the tilted angle. Primary middle ground: Miku, her face, pushing forearm, holding hand, the sliding bead and the black floor beneath her, carrying the finest linework. Secondary middle ground: the main veil, the encoder strip, the mask layers and the nearest tension weights. Tertiary layer: the remaining weights, the drifting strand, vellum tags, floating slabs and the wireframe band. Use a medium-wide lens from a slightly low position. Place her just right of center, full body from boots to hair ornaments, occupying approximately thirty percent of the frame. She steps forward out of the veil with her weight on the leading leg and her back shoulder turned, her head level, both aqua eyes clearly visible.

Give Miku exactly one core action built from two contacts. Her raised right forearm pushes a bundle of glass filaments aside so they part into a narrow vertical slit around her face and chest. Her left hand, at hip height, holds a single filament that runs taut back up to the rail, and one thickened glass bead is sliding down that filament, caught a few centimeters from her fingers. The sliding bead beside her hand is the tension point. Add no second prop and no second action.

The curtain occupies approximately seventy-six percent of the canvas. Use roughly eight thousand filaments of sharply different thickness: the thickest read as clear glass rods, the middle ones as fine threads with beads, and the finest as pale hair lines. Crop the rail and the pooled hem at the frame edges so the curtain clearly exceeds the image.

Build the rail as architecture, not a rod. Use a curved pearl-white ceramic beam, cobalt enamel brackets, black hinge plates, silver tension rings, and thin gold filigree seams, then let every filament hang from an individual silver ring so the top edge becomes a dense metallic fringe. The third grows isolated beads on the filaments at a consistent height. The fourth merges beads into long vertical capsules. The fifth fuses neighbouring capsules into a continuous clear sheet. Make every band horizontally readable so the veil reads as a single process from tension to absence.

Turn the curtain into a measuring instrument. Along one mid-height band, embed a fine horizontal encoder: a continuous row of tiny dark ticks of varying length across the filaments, interrupted every twelfth thread by a slightly thicker silver ring and a small cobalt index block. This barcode-like strip must run along the veil with the same twenty-five-degree tilt, and it must be physically tied to the filaments rather than pasted on top. It is the only place where the interface becomes the material itself.

Suspend nine glass tension weights from selected filaments just below the rail as the secondary repeated sequence. Each weight is a small tapered glass form on its own thread: a plain clear drop, a drop with one cobalt core line, a drop with trapped bubbles, a frosted drop, a drop with a hairline crack, a drop reduced to a silver shell, a drop reduced to a wireframe, an empty silver ring, and finally an empty ring holding only a shadow. Preserve her unmistakable canonical identity: luminous aqua eyes, straight aqua bangs, extremely long aqua twin tails, black-and-magenta square hair ornaments, youthful anime facial structure, slim proportions, and a clearly recognizable Hatsune Miku silhouette. sections.s02_camera: Use a side-on camera at her shoulder height, with the leaf plane almost parallel to the picture plane and the projection wall behind it. Her weight rests on the back leg; her front foot is turned toward the leaf. Do not let the leaf hide her body.
sections.s03_action: Give her exactly one core action. Her right hand holds a thin silver vein probe flat against the leaf surface and drags it slowly along the main vein; a short cyan glow trails the probe tip and the vein behind it lights up in sequence. sections.s04_motif: Construct the dominant visual object as one colossal translucent leaf occupying approximately seventy-six percent of the canvas, taller than Miku and cropped by the top, right and bottom edges. The leaf must read as a specimen grown and mounted inside a machine, with the clamp clearly mechanical.
sections.s05_material: Organize seven stages along the midrib from the clamp outward as a material progression. The first is clear glass with a bright core. The second carries internal bubbles. The third becomes frosted with pale cyan veins. The fourth thins into a silver wireframe. The fifth reduces to a cyan contour. The sixth becomes a cluster of cobalt pixels. The seventh disappears into a clean white gap in the blade. Keep the stages evenly spaced so the eye reads one continuous process along the vein.
sections.s07_subseq: Add eight small silver vein clips along the secondary veins as a quiet secondary sequence: glazed, hairline-cracked, half frosted, thin shell, wireframe outline, cyan contour, empty clip, and one clip with nothing but a shadow. Arrange them so their spacing widens toward the outer edge and never looks like a ladder.
sections.s11_costume: Dress Miku in an original white, graphite, cobalt and aqua survey suit derived from her recognizable virtual-singer design logic. Use a fitted sleeveless upper structure, a short asymmetric skirt of pearl-white ceramic panels over a translucent cyan underlayer, black thigh-high elements with thin cobalt seams, one detached sleeve printed with fine vein-line patterns on the probing arm, a bare forearm on the open side, and three small magenta fastening points. sections.s12_env: Build the environment as an infinite pure-white chamber with no walls, horizon or landscape, but give the projection one large flat receiving surface: a pale plaster wall panel standing behind the leaf and cropped by the frame. Add a tall cobalt rectangle beyond it, a matte-black horizontal beam low behind both, and two floating white slabs near the upper right. Preserve approximately thirty percent clean white negative space in the upper left, between her head and the leaf, and at the outer edge of the projection.
sections.s13_palette: Use the archive's established color hierarchy. Approximately sixty-eight percent of the image is pure white, pearl white and pale silver. Sixteen percent is cobalt blue and deep ultramarine. Ten percent is aqua and icy cyan. Five percent is black and graphite. No more than one percent is vivid magenta, reserved for registration offsets and the costume fasteners. sections.s16_mask: Apply layered inverse-color masks. sections.s20_type: Add a small, controlled typography system. sections.s05_material: Organize the five sepal rings into a material progression that recedes from the foreground to the white far end. The nearest is fully glazed ceramic with a hard specular lip. sections.s16_mask: Apply layered inverse-color masks. Preserve her unmistakable canonical identity: luminous aqua eyes, straight aqua bangs, extremely long aqua twin tails, black-and-magenta square hair ornaments, youthful anime facial structure, slim proportions, and a clearly recognizable Hatsune Miku silhouette. She must remain visually dominant and must never be replaced by a generic cyberpunk girl or a realistic human.

Use a one-point perspective camera placed low in the corridor and offset about ten degrees to the right, so the vanishing point sits left of centre and the corridor reads as architecture rather than a tunnel graphic. Put Miku in the middle third, walking toward the camera, full body from boots to hair ornaments, occupying approximately thirty-four percent of the canvas. Her head is lifted, both aqua eyes clearly visible, her stride open with the front heel just landing. Do not let any sepal hide her torso.

Give her exactly one core action built from two contacts. Her right palm presses flat against the nearest sepal edge, fingers spread along its inner curve. Her left hand carries a small pearl-white light box at hip height, its lid closed and one thin cyan seam showing. The gap between her landing heel and the floor is the tension point. Add no second prop and no second action.

Construct the dominant visual object as a colossal corridor made of five curved sepal blades rising from the floor and closing overhead into a vault, occupying approximately seventy-six percent of the canvas and cropped by the left, right and top edges. Each blade is a thick pearl-white ceramic shell on the outside and translucent aqua glass on the inside, with a polished rolled lip, cobalt collar rings at its base, silver tension cables running along its inner curve, and a fine gold seam where ceramic meets glass. The corridor must read as a grown structure braced by machine fittings.

Organize the five sepal rings into a material progression that recedes from the foreground to the white far end. The nearest is fully glazed ceramic with a hard specular lip. The second is half frosted. The third is clear glass with visible internal bubbles. The fourth is a silver wireframe of the same silhouette. The fifth is only a cyan contour line, so the corridor opens into pure white space instead of a wall. Each ring keeps an identical silhouette so the change reads as state, not shape.

Give every ring its own threshold interface. On the inner face of each sepal lip, place a thin cobalt index ring, a row of white radial ticks, a black calibration arc and a short cyan waveform band, and let the detail simplify with depth: the nearest ring carries full instrumentation, the second half, the third only ticks, the fourth only a single arc, the fifth nothing at all. All markings must follow the lip's curvature and must be interrupted where Miku or her hair passes in front of them.

Add a secondary repeated sequence of nine diagnostic plates mounted along the two lower sepal walls, receding with the corridor and shrinking in perspective. Three of them show sepal cross-sections, one shows a projected vein map from the previous record, and the last and smallest holds a single fragment of Miku's aqua eye. Keep every plate thin, semi-transparent and clearly subordinate to the architecture.

Keep the mechanical wings folded tight against her back so the corridor dominates: the left one solid pearl-white ceramic with closed black hinges and cobalt edge plates, the right one transparent with silver ribs and one glass membrane panel. Let the lowest tip of the solid wing brush the floor and cast a small hard shadow. The wings must never spread into a symmetrical angel pose.

Establish readable occlusion. The nearest sepal lip crosses in front of her right shoulder and behind her pressing palm. Two silver tension cables pass in front of the third ring and behind the second. Her nearer twin tail falls across the nearest collar ring and disappears behind it. The light box is fully unoccluded. Nothing may cover her face or the palm pressed on the sepal.

Let her hair stream backward into the corridor. The upper twin tail rises behind her head and is cropped by the nearest lip. The lower twin tail trails back through the second and third rings, doubles inside the clear third ring, and ends as three thin cyan contours near the fourth wireframe ring. Keep the hair dense and recognizable near her head.

Dress Miku in an original white, graphite, cobalt and aqua corridor suit derived from her recognizable virtual-singer design logic. Use a fitted sleeveless upper structure with a high collar, a short asymmetric skirt of pearl-white ceramic panels over a translucent cyan underlayer, black thigh-high elements with thin cobalt seams, one detached sleeve with clear glass inserts on the pressing arm, a bare forearm on the carrying side, and three small magenta fastening points. Add a narrow silver waist rail for the light box and keep the outfit precise and light.

Build the environment as an infinite pure-white chamber beyond the corridor. The floor is pale polished stone that receives one long elliptical pool of light from the corridor throat, and the space outside the sepals stays empty white with a single tall cobalt rectangle standing far to the right, a matte-black horizontal beam low behind the corridor and two floating white slabs near the upper left. Preserve approximately twenty-eight percent clean white negative space, concentrated at the far end of the corridor and along the upper corners.

Use the archive's established color hierarchy. Approximately sixty-eight percent of the image is pure white, pearl white and pale silver. Sixteen percent is cobalt blue and deep ultramarine. Ten percent is aqua and icy cyan. Five percent is black and graphite. No more than one percent is vivid magenta, reserved for registration offsets, one plate border and the costume fasteners. The sepal ceramics must stay pearl white and the inner glass aqua; no ochre, olive, brown or warm beige may appear anywhere.

Apply layered inverse-color masks. Place one broad translucent cyan mask across the third clear ring so its darker interior becomes a white knockout, one cobalt inverse plane behind the second ring, and two sharp white knockout strips cutting across the fourth wireframe ring. Where her lower twin tail crosses a cyan mask, convert it into a white silhouette with a thin aqua outline. Masks may cover outer hair, skirt plates, legs, sepal surfaces, rings and plate edges, but never her face, both eyes, her pressing palm or the light box.

Integrate a restrained glitch collage. Around the fifth contour ring, the smallest diagnostic plate, the trailing end of the lower twin tail and the outer edge of the nearest sepal, add horizontal scan slices, pixel displacement, cyan and magenta channel misregistration, erased white blocks, photocopy grain and duplicated contour echoes. The corridor's geometry, her body and her hands must stay coherent, and no glitch may enter the clean far end of the corridor.

Add a small, controlled typography system. Include the exact readable text “CALYX CORRIDOR” set vertically along the inner face of the nearest sepal, following its curve, with one tension cable crossing a letter without making the word unreadable. Place “SEPAL / PHASE 10” in small condensed cobalt lettering on the base collar of the second ring. Add one outlined “39” emblem inside a cobalt square on the floor beside her landing heel. Include no other required readable words.

Light the image from the far end of the corridor as well as from above: a soft cold white daylight pouring in through the open fifth ring, a broad shadowless light from the ceiling gap, and a faint aqua glow inside the third glass ring that reaches her hands and jaw. Let each sepal ring cast its own thin shadow ring onto the floor so the corridor's depth is measured twice, once by geometry and once by light. Avoid warm light, fog, haze, bloom, star particles and muddy grey shadows.

Maintain five readable depth layers. Foreground: the nearest lip, one cropped sepal base and the light box. Primary middle ground: Miku, her face, her pressing palm and her landing foot with the sharpest detail. Secondary middle ground: the second and third rings, the diagnostic plates and the tension cables. Tertiary layer: the fourth wireframe ring, the trailing hair and the smallest plate. Background: the fifth contour ring, the white far end, the cobalt rectangle and the floating slabs.

Render the result as a high-end two-dimensional anime key visual combining crisp character linework, pure-white editorial space, cobalt screen-print planes, pearl ceramic shells, translucent glass interiors with internal bubbles, frosted diffusion, silver wireframe, fine gold seams, threshold interface rings, halftone fragments, subtle paper grain, clean vector edges, selective photobashing, restrained dry-brush erosion and polished game-promotion art direction. Give the finest linework to Miku's face, pressing palm and landing foot, the richest material work to the nearest lip and the third glass ring, the strongest graphic rhythm to the five rings, and the most restrained treatment to the far end.

No additional physical characters, no duplicated Miku, no second face, no natural plant, no soil, no brown or earthy tones, no realistic greenhouse, no generic cyberpunk city, no symmetrical angel pose, no spread wings, no feathered wings, no portrait panels over her, no text over her face, no short hair, no missing twin tails, no distorted hands, no random letters, no uncontrolled glitch, no muddy background, no rainbow lighting. Preserve a strict hierarchy: Miku's face and the light box first, her pressing palm and landing foot second, the five sepal rings and their threshold interfaces third, the diagnostic plates and trailing hair fourth, then the typography and the pure-white far end.

The final image should feel like the archive's tenth experiment: the leaf of PHASE 09 has rolled itself into a corridor of five sepals, each ring carrying less instrumentation than the one in front of it, the far end opening into white instead of a wall, and Hatsune Miku walks out of it with one palm on the shell and a closed light box at her hip while the floor measures the corridor twice over. Pure-white abstract technology chamber, monumental five-ring sepal corridor, threshold ring interfaces, folded asymmetric wings, receding diagnostic plates, blue-white palette, controlled glitch collage, disciplined negative space, sophisticated anime presentation, premium Krea 2 game key visual and an extremely polished, completely original spatial arrangement.

seeds.title: POLLEN STORM

sections.s01_concept: Create a wide 16:9 premium sci-fi game key visual titled “POLLEN STORM”, the eleventh record of the Zero-Day Garden archive, featuring Hatsune Miku as the only physical character standing inside a white chamber filled with millions of suspended glass microspheres held in place by an invisible electrostatic field. Preserve her unmistakable canonical identity: luminous aqua eyes, straight aqua bangs, extremely long aqua twin tails, black-and-magenta square hair ornaments, youthful anime facial structure, slim proportions, and a clearly recognizable Hatsune Miku silhouette. She must remain visually dominant against the particle field and must never be replaced by a generic cyberpunk girl or a realistic human.
sections.s02_camera: Use a medium-wide camera at her eye level, tilted down only about ten degrees, so the floor and the field both read. Place Miku slightly left of centre, full body from boots to hair ornaments, occupying approximately thirty-two percent of the canvas, standing with her feet apart and her weight centred. Her head is level, both aqua eyes clearly visible, her expression composed and attentive. Keep a clean spherical void of empty air around her whole body, roughly one and a half times her height in radius, so she never dissolves into the particle noise.
sections.s03_action: Give her exactly one core action. Her left palm is raised open at chest height, and the microspheres part around it in a thin clear ring. Her right hand pinches one single sphere between thumb and forefinger at the height of her collarbone, and that sphere is visibly denser and brighter than every other sphere in the frame. The pinched sphere is the tension point. Add no second prop and no second action.
sections.s04_motif: Construct the dominant visual object as the particle field itself, occupying approximately seventy-four percent of the canvas. Use only three sphere sizes, strictly separated: large anchor spheres about the size of a fist, medium spheres the size of a thumb joint, and fine dust far smaller than a grain of rice. Every sphere is clear glass with a thin bright rim, a soft internal caustic and a tiny specular point. Do not let the sizes blur together, and do not let the field become a uniform fog.
sections.s05_material: Organize nine marked spheres into a material progression along one visible drift line that runs from the floor emitter up past her raised palm. The first is clear with a bright core. The second carries internal bubbles. The third is frosted. The fourth is half clear and half wireframe. The fifth is pure silver wireframe. The sixth reduces to a cyan contour. The seventh becomes a cluster of cobalt pixels. The eighth is a clean white gap in the field. The ninth is absent, leaving only a small bracket mark floating in the air. Space them so the drift line reads as one process.
sections.s06_sequence: Add a secondary sequence of eight silver collection rings threaded onto a vertical rail behind Miku, each holding a different quantity of captured spheres: full, three quarters, half, one quarter, a thin film, a wireframe ring, a cyan contour ring, and an empty ring with a shadow. Keep them small and quiet so they punctuate the field without competing with it.
sections.s10_hair: Let her hair cut through the field. The upper twin tail rises into the shell lattice and clears a narrow tunnel through it. The lower twin tail falls across the floor emitter, and where it crosses the emitter's cyan arc the hair turns into a white inverse silhouette with a thin aqua outline, then reappears normal below the arc. Keep the hair dense and recognizable near her head.
sections.s11_costume: Dress Miku in an original white, graphite, cobalt and aqua field suit derived from her recognizable virtual-singer design logic. Use a fitted sleeveless upper structure with a high collar, a short asymmetric skirt of pearl-white ceramic panels over a translucent cyan underlayer, black thigh-high elements with thin cobalt seams, detached sleeves with clear glass inserts and silver cuffs, a narrow aqua waist band, and three small magenta fastening points. Add a thin silver collar gauge at the throat and keep the whole costume sealed and precise rather than armoured.
sections.s12_env: Build the environment as an infinite pure-white chamber. Add a pale polished stone floor with a wide engraved cobalt ring, one tall cobalt rectangle standing far behind her, a matte-black horizontal beam low across the back, two floating white slabs near the upper right, and one thin translucent panel beyond the emitters. Preserve approximately twenty-six percent clean white negative space, concentrated in the void around her body, at the upper left and at the far right margin beyond the field.
sections.s13_palette: Use the archive's established color hierarchy. Approximately sixty-eight percent of the image is pure white, pearl white and pale silver. Sixteen percent is cobalt blue and deep ultramarine. Ten percent is aqua and icy cyan. Five percent is black and graphite. No more than one percent is vivid magenta, reserved for registration offsets, one emitter strip and the costume fasteners. The field must stay white-glass and cyan; no ochre, olive, brown or warm beige may appear anywhere.
sections.s16_mask: Apply layered inverse-color masks. Place one broad translucent cyan mask across the lower third of the field so the densest shell becomes a white knockout, one cobalt inverse plane behind the upper shell lattice, and three sharp white knockout wedges cutting through the field where the emitters are strongest. Where her lower twin tail crosses the floor emitter's arc, keep the white inverse silhouette. Masks may cover outer hair, skirt plates, legs, wing edges, field shells and emitter faces, but never her face, both eyes, her raised palm or the pinched sphere.
sections.s20_type: Add a small, controlled typography system. Include the exact readable text “POLLEN STORM” in a narrow uppercase sans serif along the inner face of the overhead emitter ring, following its curve and cropped slightly by the frame. Place “FIELD / PHASE 11” in small condensed cobalt lettering on the floor emitter's outer band. Add one outlined “39” emblem inside a cobalt square near the lower left floor ring. Include no other required readable words.
sections.s21_light: Light the image with three sources: a broad nearly shadowless white architectural light from above, a cold cyan charge glow from the three emitter rings, and a very faint internal glow inside the pinched sphere. Let millions of microspheres throw a fine shimmering caustic lattice across the floor and onto Miku's arms and skirt, and let the emitter rings cast three hard circular shadows that overlap into a single bright band. Avoid warm light, fog, haze, bloom, sparkle effects and muddy grey shadows.
sections.s22_layers: Maintain five readable depth layers. Foreground: three anchor spheres, one cropped emitter pin and the raised palm's clear ring. Primary middle ground: Miku, her face, her hands and the pinched sphere with the sharpest detail. Secondary middle ground: the shell lattice, the three emitters and the open wings. Tertiary layer: the collection rings, the drift line of marked spheres and the finer dust. Background: the cobalt rectangle, floating slabs, the black beam and the white chamber.
sections.s24_constraint: No additional physical characters, no duplicated Miku, no second face, no portrait panels, no snow, no rain, no confetti, no bubbles in water, no underwater scene, no natural plant, no soil, no brown or earthy tones, no generic cyberpunk city, no symmetrical angel pose, no feathered wings, no short hair, no missing twin tails, no distorted hands, no blurred face, no text over her face, no random letters, no uncontrolled glitch, no muddy background, no rainbow lighting, no excessive bloom, no excessive sparkles. Preserve a strict hierarchy: Miku's face and the pinched sphere first, her raised palm and the clear ring second, the shell lattice and the three emitters third, the open wings and the collection rings fourth, then the typography and the white void.
sections.s25_closing: The final image should feel like the archive's eleventh experiment: the corridor's sampling chamber has opened and its pollen is loose in a controlled storm, the microspheres obey an invisible electrostatic grid and lock themselves into eight concentric shells, the collector wing catches them in ordered rows while the solid wing pushes them aside, and Hatsune Miku stands in a perfect sphere of still air pinching one single grain between two fingers. Pure-white abstract technology chamber, monumental glass particle field, shell-lattice interface drawn by the particles themselves, asymmetric open wings, three emitter rings, blue-white palette, controlled glitch collage, disciplined negative space, sophisticated anime presentation, premium Krea 2 game key visual and an extremely polished, completely original spatial arrangement.

extra: Make the field readable as structure rather than weather. Where the field is strong, the spheres lock into eight concentric shells around the chamber's centre, each shell a loose spherical lattice with visible gaps. Where the field weakens toward the frame edges, the shells break into drifting arcs and finally into sparse scatter. The shells must be legible as geometry in the middle of the image and only dissolve at the outer margins.

Place three electrostatic emitter rings in the architecture: one wide ring embedded in the floor, one narrower ring hanging overhead and cropped by the top edge, and one vertical half-ring fixed to the wall behind her. Each emitter is a pearl-white ceramic torus with cobalt cladding, silver contact pins, a thin cyan arc of charge on its inner face, and one segmented progress strip. Let the cyan arc be the only saturated blue in the middle of the field.

Open both mechanical wings in this record, but give them opposite behaviour. The left wing is solid pearl-white ceramic with black hinges and cobalt edge plates; the spheres bounce off it and leave a clean crescent of empty air along its leading edge. The right wing is transparent with silver ribs and glass membrane panels; the spheres cling to its membrane in neat rows aligned with the ribs, so the wing looks like a collector plate. They must never form a symmetrical angel pose, and neither may cover her face or hands.

Establish readable occlusion. Three large anchor spheres pass in front of her raised palm while two of them pass behind it. One emitter pin crosses in front of her nearer twin tail. The pinched sphere in her right hand must remain completely unoccluded and perfectly sharp against the softer field behind it.

Integrate a restrained glitch collage. Around the seventh marked sphere, the outer scatter at the right margin, the trailing end of the lower twin tail and the far edge of the transparent wing, add horizontal scan slices, pixel displacement, cyan and magenta channel misregistration, erased white blocks, photocopy grain and duplicated contour echoes. The shell lattice, her body and her hands must stay geometrically clean, and no glitch may enter the void around her.

Render the result as a high-end two-dimensional anime key visual combining crisp character linework, pure-white editorial space, cobalt screen-print planes, clear glass microspheres with thin bright rims and internal caustics, pearl ceramic emitters, frosted diffusion, silver wireframe, fine gold pins, shell-lattice geometry, halftone fragments, subtle paper grain, clean vector edges, selective photobashing, restrained dry-brush erosion and polished game-promotion art direction. Give the finest linework to Miku's face and both hands, the most detailed particle work to the pinched sphere and the three nearest anchor spheres, the strongest graphic rhythm to the shell lattice and the emitter rings, and the most restrained treatment to the outer scatter.

seeds.title: SECOND SPECIMEN

sections.s01_concept: Create a wide 16:9 premium sci-fi game key visual titled “SECOND SPECIMEN”, the twelfth record of the Zero-Day Garden archive, featuring Hatsune Miku as the only physical character standing outside a thick glass observation partition, looking in at a second specimen that exists only as a scanned body. Preserve her unmistakable canonical identity: luminous aqua eyes, straight aqua bangs, extremely long aqua twin tails, black-and-magenta square hair ornaments, youthful anime facial structure, slim proportions, and a clearly recognizable Hatsune Miku silhouette. She is the only human figure in the image, and no second person may appear inside the case.
sections.s02_camera: Use an eye-level camera placed square to the partition, with a very slight angle so the glass thickness reads. Put Miku on the right side of the frame, full body from boots to hair ornaments, occupying approximately thirty-four percent of the canvas, standing close to the glass with her weight on both feet. Her head is turned toward the specimen on her left in a three-quarter view, both aqua eyes clearly visible, her expression quiet and unreadable. Do not let the partition hide her face or her raised hand.
sections.s03_action: Give her exactly one core action. Her left palm presses flat against the glass at shoulder height, fingers spread, and a faint condensation halo slowly forms around the palm from her body heat. Her right hand, at hip height, holds a small glass slide between thumb and forefinger, tilted so one edge catches the light. The single point where her palm meets the glass is the tension point. Add no second prop and no second action.
sections.s04_motif: Construct the second specimen on the far side as a scanned glass body, never as a person. It is a standing organism about two and a half metres tall, built from a thick glass stem, four curled tendrils, a cluster of sealed pods at its base and one empty ring at the top where a head would be.
